reason: Verify implementation uses the agreed domain vocabulary and relationships.
Verify behavior, boundaries, out-of-scope items, and testing decisions against the PRD.
Check that White-Box Assessment remains independent from Scan lifecycle and statistics.
Check that findings and Markdown documents are grounded in structured evidence.
Check layer boundaries and persistence responsibilities.
Check CMDB writes, actor_id filtering, migrations, candidate/asset separation, and vulnerability metrics isolation.
Check that prompt drafts and document-guided verification integrate with Scan only where required.
Check live-target verification respects high-risk guardrails.
Check archive/analyzer/tool paths avoid unsafe subprocess and network behavior.
Check any skill-facing additions satisfy metadata, schema, output, error, and raw-log contracts.
Check expert-agent routing additions, if any, follow YAML registry boundaries.
Check prompt draft behavior does not bypass existing prompt/session patterns.
Check notification and lifecycle event payloads are versioned and cross-layer consistent.
Check Markdown artifact generation follows canonical rendering principles where applicable.
Check large evidence/log/document payloads stay on disk with bounded summaries.
Check classified, sanitized failures across APIs, integrations, and tasks.
Check backend quality, security, persistence, and test coverage expectations.
Check frontend hard rules and required quality gates.
Check TypeScript strictness, TSDoc exports, component size, tests, and forbidden patterns.
Check new workspace navigation and view hierarchy changes fit the shell contract.
Check UI uses semantic tokens and severity palette.
Check confirmation, prompt draft, chat handoff, and evidence display patterns.
Check no banned visualization dependency is introduced.
Check API/service/database/frontend formats survive round-trip and validation is placed correctly.
Check implementation reuses existing patterns and avoids duplicated constants or utilities.
